phrases.example:
Provider: "Can you send that refill request before noon?"
You: "10-4 — I'll take care of it."

phrases.meaning: Let's briefly connect or discuss something.
phrases.example: Supervisor: "Let's touch base after your shift about the backlog."
"I'll circle back with billing once I have the invoice number."
"I'm slammed this hour — can we circle back at 3 PM Central?"

phrases.meaning: As soon as possible (polite urgency, not panic).
phrases.example: "Can you confirm the pharmacy received it ASAP?"
Patient: "Sorry I'm late." You: "No worries — thanks for calling."

phrases.meaning: Send me an email (casual but normal at work).
phrases.example: "Shoot me an email with the receipt and I'll loop in Accounts."

phrases.meaning: Own the task end-to-end; follow through.
phrases.example: "Can you take ownership of this portal message until it's resolved?"
"Heads up — the provider is running 15 minutes behind today."

phrases.meaning: You noticed something important — well done.
phrases.example: "Good catch on the wrong state on that intake form."

phrases.meaning: Can you handle this now? (Not literal jumping.)
phrases.example: "Can you jump on this refill before the pharmacy closes?"

phrases.meaning: Often a soft no — don't push hard; offer info and follow up.
phrases.example: Patient: "I'll think about it." You: "Of course — I'll send a summary email if helpful."

trivia.prompt: Which state is known as the Lone Star State?
trivia.fact: Texas uses Central Time for most of the state (El Paso area is Mountain).

trivia.prompt: What is the capital of California?
trivia.fact: Sacramento — not LA. Siya serves patients statewide in CA remotely.

trivia.prompt: Dallas, Texas is mainly in which US time zone?
trivia.fact: Central Time (CT). India is typically 10.5–11.5 hours ahead of CT depending on DST.

trivia.prompt: When is Thanksgiving in the US?
trivia.fact: Many patients and clinics have altered schedules that week.

choices: Military members who died in service
trivia.fact: Last Monday in May — federal holiday; expect slower responses.

trivia.prompt: Daylight saving time in most US states means…
choices: Clocks spring forward 1 hour in spring, fall back in fall
The whole country stops using time zones
India and the US always share the same clock
trivia.fact: Arizona (most) and Hawaii don't observe DST — always confirm patient timezone.

trivia.prompt: Which US holidays often affect patient availability?
choices: Thanksgiving week, Christmas, New Year's, July 4
trivia.fact: Clinics may be closed or short-staffed; set expectations kindly.

trivia.prompt: What is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania?
trivia.fact: PA is a Siya service state — use full state name in patient-facing copy when possible.

healthTerms.plain: The patient's medical record in the EHR (not a paper chart on the wall).
Renewing a medication the patient already takes — often needs provider approval.
Fixed amount the patient pays at visit/pharmacy per their insurance plan.
Insurance approval before certain meds or tests — can delay timelines.
Licensed clinician (MD, NP, PA, etc.) — not the same as "insurance provider."
Return visit or check-in after initial care — often on a subscription cadence at Siya.
Ongoing general medical home — different from specialty ADHD or weight programs.
Walk-in style acute care — not ER; not always a substitute for telehealth follow-up.

healthcareLines.line: Thank you for calling Siya Health. How may I help you today?
healthcareLines.tip: Warm, brief — Americans expect a thank-you and a clear offer to help.
Confirm identity per policy, then: "Let me pull up your chart."

healthcareLines.line: Let me pull up your chart.
healthcareLines.tip: Never discuss PHI until you've verified the right patient.

scenarios.prompt: A patient says: "I'm frustrated." What is the best first reply?
choices: "I hear you — I'm here to help. Can you tell me what happened?"
scenarios.explain: Acknowledge emotion, stay professional, gather facts — escalate clinical issues to the provider.

scenarios.prompt: Which closing is normal and professional in US healthcare email?
scenarios.explain: Please, thank you, and appreciate your help are standard — not fake politeness.

complianceQuick.prompt: Can you text PHI (patient name + diagnosis) to a provider on your personal phone?
choices: No — use approved secure channels only
Yes, if you delete it after
complianceQuick.explain: Use Spruce/EHR/approved tools. No PHI in this assistant chat either.

aiTips: Ask AI for a **checklist**, not a novel — e.g. "10 pre-publish QA bullets for a patient Instagram caption."
Paste **de-identified** scenarios only — no patient names or MRNs.
For Excel/Sheets: "Explain this formula in plain English" beats "fix my sheet" with no context.
End prompts with **format** — "Reply as 5 bullets for my supervisor."
